data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test is installed in the same mutation-testing ritual that generates its failure cases, because the guard's existence alters the set of mutations that can be planted without the author noticing.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutation set is generated by an independent process that cannot see the test","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author plants mutations mechanically without understanding the code","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the test is written before any mutation framework exists","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the result distribution matches what an independent oracle would produce","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When a test is written under the 'shown-to-fail-first' installation discipline, the author must plant a mutation that makes the test fail before seeing the test pass. This creates a selection effect: only mutations that are legible to the author's current model of the code get planted. The test therefore constrains the space of mutations that can be observed, rather than independently describing pre-existing behavior.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
